samples.summary: New render-deferral wrapper around `requestRender` has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff introduces a `requestRender` wrapper (text-editor.ts:718-724) that swallows every interior render while `undoUnitDepth > 0` and replays it once in `withUndoUnit`'s `finally` (3819-3822). Grepping the whole repo for `withUndoUnit|renderAfterUndoUnit|undoUnitDepth|hostRequestRender` returns hits only in src/view/text-editor.ts — no test file references them. The only new tests (editor-undo-selection.test.ts #1045 block, yorkie-doc-store.test.ts) assert store contents and undo-stack depth; none observe paint. If the replay ever fails to fire (e.g. depth never returning to 0, or the flag being cleared on the wrong path), every keystroke, Enter, paste and IME commit would leave the canvas stale — highly user-visible — and nothing in the suite would go red.

samples.summary: Doc claims paste is now "One undo unit … Pinned by editor-undo-selection.test.ts", but that test only asserts the cost is ≤ 6 and constant
samples.evidence: applyPastePlan's docstring was rewritten from "Not one undo unit" to "One undo unit … Pinned by `tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts`". That test (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:200-220) asserts only `expect(large).toBe(small)` and `expect(small).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6)` — it passes identically whether a paste costs 1 unit or 4, so the newly-claimed one-unit property is not pinned and a regression back to multiple `doc.update()`s per paste is invisible. The test was not updated in this diff. Additionally every paste in that test uses a *collapsed* selection, so the newly-batched "delete selection + paste" combination (the case that can overflow the 50-entry cap and lose the replaced content, exactly the #1045 failure mode) is never exercised.
searchedFor: read editor-undo-selection.test.ts multi-block paste undo cost describe block
grep for other paste undo tests in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs

samples.summary: The #1045 undo tests never check that undo restores the pre-edit caret/selection, the rule `withUndoUnit` documents as load-bearing
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s docstring (text-editor.ts:3807-3811) states that `saveSnapshot()` must stay outside the batch or undo restores the post-edit caret (presence writes inside a batch are dropped by `skipNonHistoryPresence`). The new tests assert only `texts()` (lines 294, 308, 322) and stack depth; none assert `editor.getActiveSelection()`/cursor after undo. Moving a `saveSnapshot()` inside a unit in any of the seven new call sites would silently break caret restoration with the whole suite green. The #340 test covers only the toolbar style path, not the typing/backspace/Enter/paste paths this diff changed.
searchedFor: grep getActiveSelection / getPresenceCursorPos in frontend docs tests

samples.summary: Enter-over-selection, page-break, programmatic paste-text and Hangul-commit-over-selection batching are newly added and untested
samples.evidence: Five more call sites gained `withUndoUnit` (handleEnter cell branch 2633, handleEnter top-level 2656, handlePageBreak 2696, clipboard-text paste 4221, Hangul commit 5856). The only new editor-level tests cover typing a character and Backspace over a select-all. No test asserts these paths cost one undo unit or that one undo restores the pre-edit content — e.g. Enter over a 100-block selection can still blow Yorkie's 50-entry cap if the batching regresses there. Searched frontend/tests/app/docs and packages/docs/test for undo-count assertions on Enter/page-break/IME paths and found none.
searchedFor: grep getUndoStackForTest|undo() in packages/docs and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs

samples.summary: Undo-floor cap test counts undos but never checks the undos actually restored anything
samples.evidence: The new test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:365-386) drives `while (store.canUndo()) store.undo()` and asserts `undone === 50`. It asserts nothing about document state, so it verifies only the arithmetic of `canUndo()`; a `canUndo()` that returned true 50 times while `undo()` was a no-op or corrupted content would pass. Adding one content assertion (e.g. the block's text after draining the stack) would make it exercise the reachability property it is named for.

verdict.reason: The docstring at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1514-1524 claims applyPastePlan's "One undo unit" property is pinned by tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts, but that test (lines 200-220) only asserts large===small and small<=6, which holds whether a paste costs 1 or 4 units — removing withUndoUnit from applyPastePlan (:1533) would not fail it. The test file's own header (:132-147) still asserts the pre-change belief ("constant, but *not* to one"), showing it was not updated. Its pasteHtml helper (:182-198) always uses a collapsed selection, so the batched deleteSelection+paste combination is never exercised. I searched wide for a counterexample: every repo test file containing "paste" (43+, incl. tsx/mjs) and every docs/frontend test containing "undo" (34); the docs paste tests contain no undo assertions at all; copy-integrity.test.ts:784-797's "undoable as one unit" covers a cut, not a paste; yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3174-3189 pins only the store-level insertBlocksAfter primitive and would pass with the editor's paste batching removed; docs/test/store/memory.test.ts:233-410 tests batch() generically. No Playwright/e2e suite exists. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:44-46) itself lists only the select-all+type test as planned coverage. So a changed behavior on a user path whose failure mode is the #1045 undo-cap data loss has no meaningful test, while a docstring advertises coverage that does not exist — a missing-test finding squarely in the test-adequacy lane.
